# Answers: Daily routines with reflexive verbs

## Before you start
1. The speaker gets up; "me" shows they do it to themselves. Source: [SpanishDict: Reflexive verbs](https://www.spanishdict.com/guide/reflexive-verbs)
2. "Se viste", with "se" for she and the stem change from e to i. Source: [SpanishDict: Reflexive verbs](https://www.spanishdict.com/guide/reflexive-verbs)

## Retrieval practice
1. The -se drops and comes back as a pronoun that matches the subject, before the conjugated verb: levantarse becomes me levanto. Source: [Core idea](#core-idea)
2. One model: "Me despierto a las seis. Me ducho. Me visto y desayuno. Luego salgo de casa." Other wordings are right too. Source: [Words](#words)
3. It can join the end of the infinitive, "voy a levantarme", or go before "voy": "me voy a levantar". Source: [SpanishDict: Reflexive verbs](https://www.spanishdict.com/guide/reflexive-verbs)
4. One model: "¿A qué hora te acuestas?" Source: [Words](#words)
